Sonning Common Primary School

Breakfast and After School Clubs
SCPS offer a Breakfast Club and an After School Club to help parents/carers with wrap-around childcare for their primary school age children.
Both clubs run every school day (Monday to Friday, term time only) in the School Hall and are run by NVQ3 trained staff.
Please remember to book your child into After School Club. We allow ‘on the day’ booking but we are still seeing significant numbers of children turn up without a booking. This causes us problems with ensuring appropriate staffing levels and catering. We may consider higher fees for children who are not booked in or we may turn your child away if they are not booked in.
Breakfast Club (BC) times are from 7:30am to 8:50am (start of school)
After School Club (ASC) times are from 3.20pm (end of school) to 6pm.

Fees
Breakfast Club – daily charge including breakfast
7:30am onwards £6.75 per child Breakfast Club more information
After School Club – daily charge including a hot meal after 4pm
3.20pm – 4pm £4.85 per child
3.20pm – 6.00pm £15 per child After School Club more information Due to the cost-of-living crisis, we have really tried hard to keep increases to a minimum. However, we have reached the point where we are having to put prices for wraparound care up slightly due to rises in food and energy costs.
Payments can be made via MCAS or using Childcare vouchers.
For details about the meals provided this term see the menu here Kites Kitchen After School Club Spring & Summer Menu
How to book
You MUST use MCAS to book your child into a session, as it is important for us to know whether your child is expected to attend, not only for catering purposes but more importantly for their own safety. Only children booked into the club in advance will be able to attend.
The cut off time for booking Breakfast Club is 10.00pm the evening before, and the cut off time for booking After School Club is 1.00pm on the same day.
* Should your child need to attend either club in an emergency, please call 0118 972 2105 or email office@sonning-common.oxon.sch.uk to see whether we can accept them. Do not just turn up without calling us first!
* If you need to contact the ASC before 8:30am or after 4.00pm please ring 07398 955 145
* If you have any queries regarding Breakfast or After School Club, please contact the school office on 0118 972 2105 or email office@sonning-common.oxon.sch.uk
* Our link governor for breakfast and after school club is Mark Balcon.

Attendance Expectations
Driving up attendance and tackling persistent absence is at the centre of new stronger measures launched by the Government in January 2024. You can see why being late matters.
Should you send your child to school if they are poorly?
Whilst we want to improve school attendance, children who are ill should not be in school. We especially ask that children with diarrhoea or vomiting should stay away from school until they have not been sick or had diarrhoea for at least 2 days (48 hours). If you’re not sure then you can check the NHS guidelines: Is my child too ill for school?
Helping your child with Reading
We use the Oxford Owl Read Write Inc scheme for teaching phonics and parents can access some of these Oxford Owl Read Write Inc resources and have access to the Oxford Owl eBook library. You can find more guides on helping your child with their reading on our website in Documents page for each Year group. This is a useful guide on how to help your child Enjoy Reading.
Walking to School
We encourage everyone to walk to school if they can. OCC have this useful guide on Road safety
Healthy Lunches
All KS1 children (Kites to Y2) get a free school lunch and many children in KS2 enjoy delicious Kites Kitchen lunches too. But if you are sending in a packed lunch OCC provide some guidelines on packing a healthy lunch. Recent research from Leeds University found that only one in five children had any vegetables or salad in their packed lunch. VegPower have some handy Lunchbox Hacks to help. Due to pupil allergies, we are a nut free school. Please do not include any nuts or products which contain nuts in your child’s packed lunch.
Our children, Our Future
A child friendly document from the UK Government to support teaching staff and other adults working with children who want to talk about poverty in an honest, age-appropriate and reassuring way. Child-friendly Child poverty strategy
Abuse
If you or someone you know is currently experiencing or has experienced abuse from a partner, ex-partner or family member in Oxfordshire you can speak to them using this link Domestic Abuse Support Services

Summer boredom busters
It’s the National Year of Reading, so make reading part of your summer adventures!
Why not get your child to take part in this year’s National Read-Aloud Challenge, enhance your child’s reading skills and foster a genuine passion for reading. All you need to do is set up profiles using our school’s custom URL: Readaloud Challenge.
The Sonning Common library are hosting a FREE children’s reading challenge, children across Oxfordshire can collect stickers and rewards as they enjoy reading library books. This year the Summer Reading Challenge theme is Read to the Beat, in partnership with Universal Music Group UK, celebrating the joy of reading with a theme inspired by music.
Children who finish the Challenge at an Oxfordshire library will receive a medal, a certificate and entry into a prize draw. Under 4s can take part in a mini challenge with their own special collector’s folder and stickers.
Find out more at Summer Reading Challenge and go to summerreadingchallenge.org.uk for more fun!
We’ve got our own boredom buster too: July 2026 Summer Challenge
